params.body:
## Why

A transport only became `paid` when Mollie reported a paid payment. A garage that paid by bank transfer directly, outside Mollie, had no way forward: the transport stayed in "price available" or "waiting for payment" and the only button left was to pay a second time.

## What

A platform administrator can record that a transport was paid by bank transfer (rule **S4-10.24**).

- **Who.** Administrators only. A garage gets 403, also on its own transport, and nothing changes.
- **From which states.** The model's own definition of payable (`Transport::canBeConfirmed()`): `price_available`, `price_received` or `waiting_payment`, with a price, and with two different addresses (S4-10.23). Pending, price requested, cancelled, already paid and one-address-twice are refused with 422 and the row is left exactly as it was.
- **Same path as a Mollie payment.** `TransportService::applyPayment()` and the new `markPaidByTransfer()` both end in one private `settle()`, so the state changes once, the observer mails once (garage, the selling colleague for a vehicle bought from one, the platform address) and the transport lands under "In te plannen".
- **What is recorded.** The method (`mollie_method = bank_transfer`, the one column that says how a transport was paid), who recorded it, when, and an optional note such as the transfer reference. No Mollie payment is created and Mollie is not asked anything.
- **An open checkout.** When the garage had started a checkout, it is withdrawn through the existing `MollieService::cancel()`, which only acts where `Outbound::impact('mollie')` allows and otherwise leaves the checkout to expire. A failure there does not undo the recorded payment.
- **Late reports from Mollie.** `applyPayment()` now treats a transport that is already paid as settled: paid, failed, expired or canceled reports change nothing and mail nothing. This also closes an existing gap: a repeated "paid" webhook on a transport that was already moved to a planning step set it back to `paid` and mailed again. A second payment that Mollie reports as paid on a transport settled another way is logged as a warning, because that money has to be returned.

## Screens

- Overview, row menu of a transport that waits on the garage: "Markeer als betaald (overschrijving)". It asks first through `ui.dialog`: garage, car and amount as a quiet table, one optional note field, confirm label "Markeer als betaald".
- Transport window: the same action as a secondary button left of the pay button, same dialog.
- After recording: the row shows "betaald via overschrijving" in quiet text for the administrator; the window shows a "Betaling" group (method, who recorded it and when, the note). A garage reads only the method.
- Translations in nl, fr, en, de.

## Migration

`2026_10_01_160000_a_transport_can_be_paid_by_bank_transfer`: three nullable columns on `transport` (`paid_marked_by`, `paid_marked_at`, `paid_note`). No backfill.

## Tests

`TransportPaidByBankTransferTest` (26 cases, `@rule S4-10.24`): recording from each payable state (state, method, who, when, note, mails once, listed under "In te plannen"), the seller mail, 403 for a garage, every refused state and the same-address case, recording twice, the open checkout going through the gated door only, a Mollie failure on withdrawal, nothing sent to Mollie outside production, late paid/failed/expired/canceled reports through the webhook, the return route and the pay link, a late report after a planning step, and what the row menu and the window show to an administrator and to a garage.

Full suite, PHPStan and Pint on the new files pass locally.
params.title: Record a transport paid by bank transfer, outside Mollie
